title: The Poverty of Petition and the Nature of Prayer
english: For the soul holds the starting points of the evils that are in it from the passions of the flesh. If no one is able to kill all the sinners of the earth in the manner spoken of, he will destroy from the city of the Lord all those working in lawlessness. For when the members upon the earth are put to death, the body being subdued and led away as a slave, the starting points of the sins from the flesh are no longer those which stir up in the soul thoughts rushing toward the practice of lawlessness for the sake of pleasure.

Everyone asking for something, who does not possess what he asks for by coming through the asking, is poor (Ps 101). Everyone praying to God asks for a participation in good things, which he is not able to have from himself; therefore, all are poor toward God. Even if David was great and a king, in the things given from God he was poor; therefore, having known himself to be lacking among many or all of those being supplied from God, he is filled with sorrow as if he were greatly discouraged. If, after not being thus disposed, he pours out his petition before the Lord, asking from the One giving good things to those asking Him. For the one not asking these things, but the things of the passing moments, does not have the boldness to pour out his petition before the Lord through an impassioned choice.

Prayer indeed expresses entreaty toward God and supplication, but petition expresses the request regarding which he desires to be granted to the one praying (Ps 101,2). These indeed are the truly good things, which it is fitting to give to God and beneficial for the askers to receive. If it is said regarding the cry of the saints praising God and praying to Him loudly, it is not that which is in the utterance, but the intensification of the mind.

But God turns His face away from some of those praying according to more ways than those asking [without] entreating (Ps 101,3); it is necessary for God to grant [these] and for them to receive [them] effectively, either to provide what is fitting to God to ask, not necessarily having the time to depart from these things profitably; and there are also those who happen to be worthy of these things while sinning. The holy man does not entreat saying: 'Do not, if you have changed your mind about asking such things of me, turn Your face away from me; but I pray not that I might not be afflicted (for this is impossible) but that, being afflicted, I might not [be destroyed].'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Zion and the Glory of Christ
english: That I might be defeated and not rejoice in any hope, enduring tribulations and boasting in them. For tribulation works endurance, and endurance testing, and testing hope, and hope does not put one to shame. [Ps 101:4–6] It is customary for those who are shivering to wrap themselves tightly because they are always being chilled. The smoke fails when the fire is being extinguished, and having descended into the [gap], the fire itself works [gap]. Even the days shall not fail (for it will not be good for me if the light of my days is extinguished), bring the afflictions; for if they remained, what would become of the cessation of my days, but also my bones would rather be frozen by remaining. It is often said that the bones of the inner man are the strengths of the dogmas and the powers of the soul, and they are frozen by the burning of the passions of the soul. And he says that his heart has become dry, with nothing cheerful or upon which he has acquired joy. For it has become in the coming circumstances such that it is no longer possible to feed the bread which is appropriate and fitting to his most precious essence. For to receive this bread is impossible without being surrounded and clouded by those from without. He says, moreover, that this bread has not been nourished and he has forgotten that he once tasted it. But, groaning so much because of the present painful things, I leave a fully extended and continuous groan, as if from his voice, with a wailing occurring, that my bone might be joined and in some way united to my flesh through the much approaching dryness, casting off all the moisture scattered to my body from the coming harm. For that moisture was present to me, enjoying the bone, and it draws it away from the flesh, from the middle flesh and the place having bones. [Ps 101:14] For you will have compassion on those who have suffered, since you are God, the compassionate, and long-suffering, and full of mercy, and true. And there will be a time in which the things promised concerning Zion will be fulfilled; but who is not the most blessed and most desired time, the time of the resurrection, O Lord? And I prophesy this in these words of God, of Him, the Lord...

and of our Savior Jesus Christ, the theophany into men being the cause of the rebuilding of Zion. Once having become so, do not suppose for me the city upon the earth, nor consider the earthly Jerusalem to be signifying it, but rather the renewal of the citizenship of piety.

Why has he remembered Zion alone? (Ps 101:14) For what previously had not come except toward the lost sheep of Israel. For having come into the world once for his own (for his people were being used through the fathers), he will not present any of those in the world, but with his own he will vivify the whole world. (Ps 101:16-17) When the fearing of the name of the Lord is being brought in, and the fearing of the same Lord having been perfected (for there is no lack to those fearing him), they begin even with piety, believing in his name. For after the faith into his appellation, they believe in God himself and in his Christ, a faith reckoned as righteousness, through which everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ will be born from God. And it is perfect to be born from God; therefore also sinlessness follows the being born from him.

And the Gentiles, having feared the name of the Lord, having surpassed the Gentiles, being intellectually kings by having received foolishness to reign for an eternity, fear the glory of the Lord more than his name, as it is between those fearing the name of the Lord and the Lord himself, those fearing his glory are kings reigning accordingly; as Paul writes to the Corinthians, 'For you reigned without us; and indeed you reigned, so that we also might reign with you.' (1 Cor 4:8). And perhaps according to the first visitation the Lord built Zion, but according to the second he will appear with his glory.

And not only thus: the Word having become flesh and having tabernacled among us (John 1:14), he built the church spiritually, called Zion; and he will appear in his glory, so that having tabernacled among us, we might behold his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. (Ps 101:19b, 20a) For the Gentiles were built up having believed in the Lord according to the having come to piety.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Groaning of the Bound and the Freedom of the Sons
english: For when anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; and in this Christ, the two—the one from circumcision and the one from the Gentiles—are being created into one new man. For the term 'creation' signifies not a change of substance but a change of form or a transformation. According to this, the meaning of 'O God, create in me a clean heart' (Ps 51:10) is expressed.

If this meaning applies to many things, then the Lord's saying 'I have created you as the beginning of his ways for his works' does not signify a change of substance for the person speaking; for he was not created from nothing, but as the beginning of God's ways for his works; and to be created as the beginning of these things denotes a relationship, not a change of substance. Thus, a people being created will praise the Lord, coming to the knowledge of the one God. Furthermore, the term 'being created' is used; for if he had intended a change of substance, the one being created would be called 'a people created'; for it is possible to always remain in the state of being transformed and changed rather than in the state of being a new substance.

The reason for the people being created and praising the Lord is presented in the fact that He descended from His holy height. Because He has taken the form of a servant and has descended to us even unto death, He descended from His holy height, never ceasing to be holy or to be high (Ps 101:20b, 21). Incorporeal and spiritual essence, rather, is how the Lord exists; He is not in a place, for the incorporeal is not limited by place, being uncircumscribable and beyond boundaries. Since He has become accustomed by power to all that comes from Him and is governed by Him (for He was in the world, and the world came through Him), He works within the better and more excellent parts of the world.

If it is said according to 'He who dwells in the heavens' (Ps 103:20) and 'Our Father who is in heaven' (Matt 6:9), we do not consider Him as being contained by places, but we set forth that He exists by an unutterable power toward His own works; therefore, it is said that He is in the heavens, which are the different parts of the world. For indeed, the thought of all things holds this kind of concept. Since God, not being in heaven in the manner spoken of, looks down upon the earth because of those having been made to be provided for by Him here, it is most correctly said, 'The Lord looked down from heaven upon the earth' (Ps 113:6). And the pretext through which the Word does this is...

He immediately brought forward, saying, 'Of those who hear the groans of the bound.' For those bearing the bonds and the shackles of wickedness groan out of repentance. For one used to doing evil with pleasure, he took it lightly and willingly bore the consequences following it; but others have withdrawn from the acts of wickedness, being weighed down by the hand of that evil, having been bound by it; therefore they also groan toward Him who is able to loose the bound. And the Lord, looking upon the earth, also looses the sons of the dead—that is, those born from those who practiced the sin leading to death and because of this have died. And if those coming from the Gentiles are not descendants of sinful and impious fathers, and death having prevailed has swallowed them up; whom He has freed the sons from sins, He has loosed from the bitter bonds through the mystery of rebirth. And it is possible to use these two verses for those bound in persecutions because of the word of Christ, and for the sons of those dead through the witness of the truth.

For the contemplative soul, being Zion, will see those announcing to her the teachers of the name of the Lord, and announcing also His praise in Jerusalem, which by seeing peace profits through thought. If Zion and Jerusalem were to accuse the church because of seeing the greater things and seeing peace in the harmony and the concord of the dogmas, it would follow rightly that in this so-called Zion the name of the Lord and His praise should be announced in this so-called Jerusalem. Who answered Him in the way of His strength? The word does not agree. Does he not say of the people being created, to praise the Lord? Rather, he considers the one who, being poor by predestination, is not despondent and pours out his prayer before the Lord, to be the one answering, not with voice and utterance, but walking strongly in the way of His strength and with rectitude the way of virtuous deeds. For one does not answer God only truly, but not merely with voice. He says: 'Since I have been commanded to achieve much readiness for me and to contemplate the doctrines of your most unshakeable truth, and much...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
